question: For $$f(x)=x^3-5x^2-3x$$ on $[1,3]$, verify the hypotheses of the Mean Value Theorem and find the value of $c\in(1,3)$ for which $$f'(c)=\frac{f(3)-f(1)}{3-1}.$$
explanation:
Verification of the hypotheses
The function is a polynomial, so it is continuous on $[1,3]$ and differentiable on $(1,3)$.
Average rate of change
$$f(1)=1-5-3=-7$$
and $$f(3)=27-45-9=-27.$$
Therefore, $$\frac{f(3)-f(1)}{3-1}=\frac{-27+7}{2}=-10.$$
Derivative condition
$$f'(x)=3x^2-10x-3.$$
By the Mean Value Theorem, $$3c^2-10c-3=-10.$$
Hence, $$3c^2-10c+7=0.$$
Solution for $c$
$$3c^2-10c+7=(3c-7)(c-1)=0.$$
Thus, $$c=\frac{7}{3}\quad\text{or}\quad c=1.$$
Since $c$ must lie in $(1,3)$, the required value is $$c=\frac{7}{3}.$$

options.C: The hypotheses are not satisfied because $f(1)\neq f(3)$.
